items.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Hugh Lawson, the name I couldn’t think of the other day, he was the piano player

ctx.x: Okay, we when we left off you were mentioning…and let’s just talk about Pepper and the Jones boys. I shouldn’t say the Jones boys, Elvin, Thad, where all that fits. They fit prominently in my life because they were the significant leaders in the jazz field because each had been out with somebody of note.

Pepper was the most proficient player, I mean technically, than anybody in that spectrum. He really knew music. Yusef was a student. Yusef had this thing for sound and feeling. He had this thing that he played, you know? He had the “Mournful Prayer” and all of this stuff. A lot of it was about the show. We had a great big Chinese gong on stage that was about the size of that wall. It was played with this big mallet. It would vibrate and get everybody’s attention in the neighborhood. It was like Tarzan is coming…
Well, it was a culture, a shared culture.
